title: "Average Putts Per Round on the PGA Tour"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
---

## Research Question

**How does the average number of putts per round vary among PGA Tour players, and how do the top 25 players compare?**

In professional golf, the number of putts taken per round is a fundamental measure of performance on the greens. While top players strive to minimize putts, putting averages vary substantially based on course conditions, green size, and the number of greens hit in regulation. This project investigates how tournament putting averages fluctuate across the PGA Tour and compares the distributions of the world's leading golfers.

## Putting Distributions Across the Tour

The visualization below examines **Average Putts Per Round** across **26,442 tournament observations** from the 2015 through 2023 PGA Tour seasons. The shaded band marks the middle 50% (interquartile range: 28.00 to 29.75) of all tour rounds, the dashed vertical line indicates the tour-wide median of **28.75 putts per round**, and the boxplots display the career tournament distributions for the top 25 players from the final 2024 FedExCup standings (ordered by median putts per round, with the lowest averages at the top).

```{r}
#| label: fig-putts-per-round
#| fig-cap: "Tournament Putts Per Round distributions for the Top 25 PGA Tour golfers compared to the tour-wide baseline (N = 26,442)."
#| fig-width: 8.5
#| fig-height: 7.5

library(tidyverse)

# Load official tournament Putts Per Round data (Stat 119)
pga_data <- read_csv("data/pga_putts_per_round.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# Top 25 players based on the final 2024 FedExCup standings
top25_players <- c(
  "Scottie Scheffler", "Xander Schauffele", "Hideki Matsuyama", "Keegan Bradley",
  "Ludvig Åberg", "Rory McIlroy", "Collin Morikawa", "Wyndham Clark",
  "Sam Burns", "Patrick Cantlay", "Sungjae Im", "Sahith Theegala", "Shane Lowry",
  "Adam Scott", "Tony Finau", "Byeong Hun An", "Viktor Hovland", "Russell Henley",
  "Akshay Bhatia", "Robert MacIntyre", "Billy Horschel", "Tommy Fleetwood",
  "Sepp Straka", "Matthieu Pavon", "Taylor Pendrith"
)

# Filter tournament observations for the top 25 players and order by median putts
top25_data <- pga_data |>
  filter(player %in% top25_players) |>
  group_by(player) |>
  mutate(player_median = median(putts_per_round, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(player = fct_reorder(player, -player_median))

# Calculate baseline metrics across all 26,442 tour observations
tour_median <- median(pga_data$putts_per_round, na.rm = TRUE)
tour_q25 <- quantile(pga_data$putts_per_round, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE)
tour_q75 <- quantile(pga_data$putts_per_round, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)

# Create the comparison graphic
ggplot(top25_data, aes(x = putts_per_round, y = player)) +
  # Shaded region showing the Tour middle 50% across all 26,442 rounds
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin = tour_q25, xmax = tour_q75,
    ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf,
    fill = "#e8f0ec", alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  # Dashed line at the tour median (28.75 putts/round)
  geom_vline(xintercept = tour_median, linetype = "dashed", color = "#3b6e52", linewidth = 0.7) +
  # Boxplots representing each player's tournament distribution
  geom_boxplot(
    fill = "#2d5a3f", color = "#1b3827",
    alpha = 0.75, width = 0.55,
    outlier.alpha = 0.25, outlier.size = 1.1
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(25, 33)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(25, 33, by = 1)) +
  labs(
    title = "Putts Per Round: Top 25 PGA Tour Professionals",
    subtitle = "Tournament distributions (2015–2023) vs. Tour middle 50% (shaded band) and median (dashed line, N = 26,442)",
    x = "Average Putts Per Round",
    y = NULL,
    caption = "Data: Official PGA Tour ShotLink (Stat 119, 2015–2023) | Sample: Top 25 players from 2024 FedExCup standings | Shaded band = Tour IQR (28.00–29.75)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13, color = "#1a1a1a"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9.5, color = "#4a4a4a", margin = margin(b = 10)),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 7.5, color = "#666666", margin = margin(t = 10)),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8.5),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#f2f2f2")
  )
```

## Key Findings

- **Tour-Wide Baseline:** Across all **26,442** tournament rounds analyzed, the median putting performance is **28.75 putts per round**, with the middle 50% of tournament appearances falling tightly between **28.00** and **29.75** putts per round.
- **Substantial Week-to-Week Variation:** Even the top 25 golfers in the world demonstrate considerable tournament-to-tournament variability, frequently spanning from 26 to over 31 putts per round across events.
- **Top 25 Comparisons:** Among the top 25 players, golfers such as Sahith Theegala, Wyndham Clark, and Sungjae Im maintain the lowest median putting averages (28.0 to 28.2 putts per round). Conversely, elite ball-strikers such as Collin Morikawa, Keegan Bradley, and Matthieu Pavon register higher median putting averages (29.2 to 29.5 putts per round), demonstrating that top-tier FedExCup finishes can be achieved through outstanding approach and tee-to-green play.

## Data Source

The dataset is derived from official **PGA Tour ShotLink** tournament statistics (**Stat 119: Putts Per Round**) covering the **2015 through 2023 seasons**, compiled via the open-source PGA Tour Stats repository. The dataset contains **26,442 validated tournament observations** across 997 professional golfers and 99 tour events, recording each player's total putts, rounds played, and official average putts per round per tournament.
